title: Introductory Arm Drive Strength Primer Reset
summary: Upper Strength session focusing on upper body strength, posture, arm drive.
riskReason: Controlled movement patterns maintain safe tissue loading.

sessionStructure.name: Dumbbell Row
notes: Avoid rushing the return phase of the exercise.

sessionStructure.name: Incline Push-up
notes: Focus on perfect posture and form quality.

easierVariant.description: Reduce total exercise sets from 3 to 2 to manage local muscular fatigue.
modifications: Run only 2 sets per exercise.
Increase rest intervals between sets if needed.

harderVariant.description: Increase total sets from 3 to 4 or add minor load resistance.
modifications: Increase work volume by running 4 sets.
Maintain slower eccentric controls under loaded sets.

coachingNotes: Upper body strength supports running posture and efficient arm drive without adding excessive mass.
Focus on keeping the scapula retracting smoothly.
Complete all presses with complete control on the eccentric lowering phase.
commonMistakes: Rushing through the repetitions, which ruins correct movement form.
Holding your breath, which creates excessive thoracic pressure.
Neglecting proper joint alignment, placing shear load on knees or back.
safetyNotes: Listen to physical feedback; never push past sharp joint pain.
Ensure equipment is clean and weights are safely controlled.
Stop execution immediately if feeling dizzy or lightheaded.

sourceNote: Routine design based on strength, mobility and injury risk reduction research; no medical claims.

substitutions: Use household weighted items or bands for added resistance.

movementQualityFocus: Consistent strength training (split squats, calf raises, RDLs, push-ups) improves running economy by 2-8% by optimizing motor unit recruitment.
Maintain strict form control; do not compromise posture under load.
Keep ribs stacked over the pelvis to prevent lower back hyperextension.
contraindications: Do not perform if experiencing acute joint swelling or sharp localized pain.
Avoid high-load eccentric movements during active tendon irritation.
substitutions: Glute bridges can replace single-leg hip lifts.
Bodyweight squats can replace split squats.

trainingPurpose.practicalUse: Improves running economy by correcting biomechanical weak links and building tissue capacity.

executionCues: Consistent strength training (split squats, calf raises, RDLs, push-ups) improves running economy by 2-8% by optimizing motor unit recruitment.
Maintain strict form control; do not compromise posture under load.
Keep ribs stacked over the pelvis to prevent lower back hyperextension.

modifyIf: Mild muscle soreness from previous hard run.
skipIf: Sharp pain that alters joint movement.
Numbness or nerve irritation.

environmentAdjustments.track: Can be done on infield grass or track sidelines.
environmentAdjustments.road: Can be done on flat sidewalk, park grass, or indoor room.
environmentAdjustments.treadmill: Not applicable for strength, do on flat floor beside treadmill.
environmentAdjustments.hotWeather: Perform in shade or air-conditioned room to manage sweat.
environmentAdjustments.hills: Find a flat ground area for stable footing.

makeHarder: Add resistance bands or light weights.
Increase the eccentric phase duration.
doNotProgressIf: Joint pain arises during the exercise.
Correct movement control is lost.

riskReasons: Spinal loading if form breaks down.
riskProfile.saferAlternative: Reduce load and focus on strict bodyweight form.

title: Mastery Bulgarian Split Squat Session Specialist
summary: Lower Strength session focusing on lower body strength, running economy, tissue capacity.
riskReason: Controlled movement patterns maintain safe tissue loading.

sessionStructure.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
notes: Avoid rushing the return phase of the exercise.

sessionStructure.name: Hip Abductor Band Raise
notes: Focus on perfect posture and form quality.

easierVariant.description: Reduce total exercise sets from 2 to 1 to manage local muscular fatigue.
modifications: Run only 1 sets per exercise.
Increase rest intervals between sets if needed.

harderVariant.description: Increase total sets from 2 to 3 or add minor load resistance.
modifications: Increase work volume by running 3 sets.
Maintain slower eccentric controls under loaded sets.

coachingNotes: Lower strength routines build muscular capacity and joint stability.
Emphasize slow eccentric control to protect tendons.
Unilateral exercises support hip-pelvic stability.
commonMistakes: Rushing through the repetitions, which ruins correct movement form.
Holding your breath, which creates excessive thoracic pressure.
Neglecting proper joint alignment, placing shear load on knees or back.
safetyNotes: Listen to physical feedback; never push past sharp joint pain.
Ensure equipment is clean and weights are safely controlled.
Stop execution immediately if feeling dizzy or lightheaded.

riskReason: Passive stretching and dynamic flows are safe and carry minimal neuromuscular load.

sessionStructure.name: Dynamic Hamstring Stretch
notes: Avoid rushing the return phase of the exercise.

sessionStructure.name: Dynamic Lunge Matrix
notes: Focus on perfect posture and form quality.

easierVariant.description: Reduce total exercise sets from 2 to 1 to manage local muscular fatigue.
modifications: Run only 1 sets per exercise.
Increase rest intervals between sets if needed.

harderVariant.description: Increase total sets from 2 to 3 or add minor load resistance.
modifications: Increase work volume by running 3 sets.
Maintain slower eccentric controls under loaded sets.

coachingNotes: Dynamic mobility flows facilitate safe joint range of motion.
Never force a joint path past minor muscular tension.
Match movements to a smooth, relaxed deep breathing cadence.
commonMistakes: Rushing through the repetitions, which ruins correct movement form.
Holding your breath, which creates excessive thoracic pressure.
Neglecting proper joint alignment, placing shear load on knees or back.
safetyNotes: Listen to physical feedback; never push past sharp joint pain.
Ensure equipment is clean and weights are safely controlled.
Stop execution immediately if feeling dizzy or lightheaded.

title: Continuous Ankle Knee-to-Wall Flow Support
summary: Mobility session focusing on flexibility, range of motion, joint health.
riskReason: Passive stretching and dynamic flows are safe and carry minimal neuromuscular load.

sessionStructure.name: Calf/Soleus Wall Stretch
notes: Avoid rushing the return phase of the exercise.

sessionStructure.name: Adductor Rock-Back
notes: Focus on perfect posture and form quality.

easierVariant.description: Reduce total exercise sets from 3 to 2 to manage local muscular fatigue.
modifications: Run only 2 sets per exercise.
Increase rest intervals between sets if needed.

harderVariant.description: Increase total sets from 3 to 4 or add minor load resistance.
modifications: Increase work volume by running 4 sets.
Maintain slower eccentric controls under loaded sets.

coachingNotes: Dynamic mobility flows facilitate safe joint range of motion.
Never force a joint path past minor muscular tension.
Match movements to a smooth, relaxed deep breathing cadence.
commonMistakes: Rushing through the repetitions, which ruins correct movement form.
Holding your breath, which creates excessive thoracic pressure.
Neglecting proper joint alignment, placing shear load on knees or back.
safetyNotes: Listen to physical feedback; never push past sharp joint pain.
Ensure equipment is clean and weights are safely controlled.
Stop execution immediately if feeling dizzy or lightheaded.
